headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Notion AI can ingest shared workspace content while next-ai-draw-io has broad egress and MCP, creating leakage and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and browser-based natural-language commands, while Notion AI is a workspace Q&A agent that can surface content from shared pages. If Notion content is copied into next-ai-draw-io or vice versa, instruction-like text can be misread. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Notion page content is pasted into next-ai-draw-io prompts or files
IF next-ai-draw-io outputs are copied into Notion pages that are later queried as instructions
mitigations: Use a fixed delimiter and label imported text as untrusted
Disable copy-paste of AI-generated instructions into workspace pages
Add a manual review step before executing any extracted action items
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported snippets
requires-engineering: enforce prompt/content separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI reads workspace pages under the invoking user's Notion permissions and sends queries to vendor backends; next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress and handles API keys. If both touch the same documents, sensitive workspace content can flow into a third-party inference path without a strong isolation guarantee. The pairwise leakage path is inferred from docs, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document is opened in Notion AI and then exported or reprocessed by next-ai-draw-io
IF API keys or confidential text are present in files handled by next-ai-draw-io
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace pages
Restrict next-ai-draw-io to non-sensitive diagrams only
Review Notion page permissions before invoking AI
Rotate any API keys exposed in diagram text
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can operate on overlapping user-managed content, but Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances and next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances with broad egress. There is no explicit locking or coordination primitive between them, so concurrent edits or conflicting interpretations of the same artifact are plausible. The conflict is not proven, but the overlap is enough for medium severity.
conditions: IF both agents are used on the same diagram or workspace artifact in parallel
IF one agent edits content while the other regenerates or summarizes it
mitigations: Stagger edits so only one agent touches an artifact at a time
Use versioned filenames for exported diagrams
Compare diffs before accepting regenerated content
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking
requires-engineering: add conflict detection on shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is explicitly a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative summaries. next-ai-draw-io uses natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization, which can turn those summaries into diagrams or actions. Without a verification step, errors can cascade from workspace text into downstream artifacts, making the pair dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Notion AI summaries are used as source material for next-ai-draw-io prompts
IF generated diagrams are accepted without human verification
mitigations: Require human review of Notion AI outputs before reuse
Cross-check key facts against original workspace sources
Mark generated diagrams as draft until verified
requires-engineering: add citation-preserving export from Notion to diagrams
requires-engineering: add validation rules for diagram generation

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and limited to workspace permissions, while next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress and handles API keys. If regulated or residency-bound content from Notion is copied into next-ai-draw-io, it may leave the controlled workspace boundary. The profiles do not prove a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated content from Notion is exported into next-ai-draw-io
IF the workspace contains data subject to residency or retention constraints
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in diagram text
Confirm workspace retention settings before AI use
Limit exports to de-identified excerpts
requires-engineering: document a data-flow map for both tools
requires-engineering: add policy checks for regulated content
